title: Persistent Drain: Isolated to Background Network Activity
body:
Updating my review following developer correspondence. Recommending users plug in overnight doesn't address the software issue causing 30% battery drops on an iPhone 15 (91% health).
A key finding for the dev team: the drain is tied directly to network activity.
 When tested with Wi-Fi and mobile data active, battery plummets from ~70% to 40% overnight.
 When tested completely offline (Wi-Fi and mobile data toggled off), the battery drain is drastically reduced.
While still higher than ideal, the stark difference indicates relentless background data calls or telemetry loops while idle. Please look into why the app is generating so much background data traffic overnight when it should be idle.

title: Found a Bug!
body:
I genuinely love Alarmy. I’ve been using it for a long time now, and it has helped me a lot with waking up on time. I’ve even recommended it to a few friends because it really works. Huge appreciation to the team for building such a useful app.

However, I’ve noticed a loophole that’s affecting its purpose (at least for me). Even when the snooze limit is set (for example, 2 snoozes), if I force-close the app while the alarm is ringing and then reopen it, the alarm starts ringing again — but the snooze count gets reset. This allows me to snooze again, even though I had already used up my allowed snoozes.

Unfortunately, I’ve subconsciously started using this trick and end up sleeping longer, which defeats the whole point of the app 😅

I really hope the team can fix this issue, because Alarmy works best when it’s strict. Thank you so much for your efforts and for an otherwise amazing app!
